done_when: forge merge enable's close skips the model review and instead records a clean result only after a mechanical check that the fix changes nothing but forge.toml's top-level merge setting, set to agent (every other parsed setting equal to the default branch's); any other change is refused with a plain reason and no review; tests and CI still run and the owner still merges; no other item skips review; a command test covers a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release, including a refused case with an extra change

findings.body: If the default branch contains an open spotted entry for `forge.toml` from another item, this check passes, but close subsequently changes an extra file. `src/forge/spotted.py:164` matches that entry against the generated Done-when and marks it done; `src/forge/close.py:240` invokes this logic, and line 248 commits the resulting `plans/spotted.json` change. The PR therefore receives a clean mechanical result without model review despite containing more than the merge setting and permitted fix record. A subsequent close then refuses the extra change Forge itself wrote. This is additional evidence beyond the ruling permitting only the generated fix record. Prevent spotted-list writes on this path and extend the command test to check the final published diff with an existing spotted entry.
findings.title: Not done: merge-enable close must check the final published change

why: forge merge enable runs the normal model review on its one-line forge.toml change; if that review blocks (for example on a missing proof list), no one can fix it: agents may never touch the merge setting and the owner would have to repair a change Forge wrote. Owner decision 2026-10-09: skip the model review for this change
